methodology: The study describes the synthesis of HCN-derived polymers from thermally induced bulk polymerization of DAMN at temperatures ranging from 170 to 190°C in both solid-state and melt conditions. Structural characterization was performed using various spectroscopic techniques (FTIR, NMR, XPS) and diffraction methods (XRD). The morphological and thermal stability properties were also evaluated.
research_objective: To demonstrate the robustness and straightforward nature of thermally activated polymerizations of DAMN under conditions comparable to those found in early Earth's environment, with a focus on their potential as multifunctional materials and nonenzymatic peroxide sensors.

key_findings.finding: Prebiotic chemistry inspired novel polymeric HCN-based films with potential applications, especially as multifunctional materials.
Thermally activated polymerizations of DAMN under comparable conditions to hydrothermal vents are robust and straightforward, suitable for chemical evolution research and current materials science.
Polymerization yields of DAMN polymers obtained were 88 ± 2% in both cases (DAMN polymer-SSP and DAMN polymer-MP).
The final products from the polymerizations are black.
Thermal activation of DAMN leads to HCN-derived macrostructures free of oxygen and possibly with extended two-dimensional (2-D) structures
Polymerization of DAMN results in insoluble black polymers produced by water polymerization, which can be hydrolyzed or oxidized under complex polymerization pathways [17]

Demonstrated that basic prebiotic chemistry simulation experiments under plausible early Earth environmental conditions can lead to the generation of a successful and efficient nonenzymatic sensor producible using a low-cost solvent-free process.
